step1_summary: Chief complaint: 6-week history of feeling “tired, run-down” with diffuse body aching.

Symptoms: • Onset mid-February (≈2 wks after returning from a U.S. holiday) • Generalised myalgia (shoulders, back, hips, knees) • Fatigue, reduced daytime energy/concentration • Mild, non-specific headaches • Decreased appetite but no weight change • No fever now, but mild fever/sore throat at rash onset • No respiratory, GI, GU or neurologic symptoms reported.
Skin: single annular-looking rash on back of calf mid-/late-Feb; not very itchy; faded over ≈2 wks.
Past medical history: Asthma, hay fever.
Medications/allergies: Uses preventive inhaler morning & night; OTC antihistamine. No allergies documented.
Family/social history: Works in health-tech, lives with wife, occasional alcohol, no smoking mentioned. Enjoys walking/hiking and wore shorts while in U.S. (possible tick exposure).
Vital signs / exam: None provided in transcript.
Labs/Imaging: None yet; doctor plans blood work incl. Lyme serology, CBC, renal, liver, thyroid, etc.

V: Small-vessel vasculitis (e.g., hypersensitivity vasculitis): could cause rash + systemic aches.
I: Lyme disease (Borrelia burgdorferi): erythema migrans–like calf rash after hiking; fatigue, arthralgia.
Viral infection / post-viral fatigue (EBV, CMV, parvovirus, COVID): sore throat, persistent fatigue, myalgias.
Subacute bacterial infection (e.g., endocarditis): constitutional symptoms, but no fevers/murmur reported.
N: Hematologic malignancy (lymphoma/leukemia): fatigue, possible rash, but no B-symptoms or adenopathy noted.
D: Vitamin D or iron deficiency: common, can cause fatigue & myalgias, especially in winter months.
I2: Medication side-effect (inhaled corticosteroid or antihistamine causing fatigue): unlikely but possible.
C: Hereditary connective-tissue disorders (e.g., Ehlers–Danlos) not suggested by history—listed for completeness.
A: Systemic lupus erythematosus: fatigue, arthralgia, rash, but rash location/appearance atypical.
Early rheumatoid arthritis / seronegative inflammatory arthritis: symmetrical joint aching (shoulders, knees, hips).
T: Over-use/strain from recent increased activity while travelling: could explain aches, not fatigue.
E: Adrenal insufficiency: fatigue, myalgias, but usually weight loss, hyperpigmentation, GI symptoms.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Classic timeline: hiking in endemic area → annular calf rash resembling erythema migrans → several weeks later persistent fatigue and migratory arthralgia.
supporting_evidence: Travel to U.S. with outdoor walking in shorts (tick habitat).
Single expanding, non-itchy rash that faded over 1-2 weeks (photograph shown).
Onset of fatigue and diffuse joint/muscle aching shortly after rash.
Doctor specifically considers and plans Lyme serology.
opposing_evidence: No remembered tick bite (though ≥30 % do not recall).
No neurologic (facial palsy) or cardiac (AV block) features yet.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Post-viral or chronic viral infection (e.g., EBV/CMV)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Sore throat with possible low-grade fever followed by prolonged fatigue and myalgias is common with EBV/CMV or other viral illnesses.
supporting_evidence: History of sore throat and feeling feverish around symptom onset.
Persistent tiredness and myalgias without focal findings.
opposing_evidence: Rash morphology less typical for viral exanthem (single patch).
Symptoms appearing after travel/outdoor exposure fit Lyme better.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Common endocrine cause of fatigue and generalized aches; should be screened via TSH in routine bloods.
opposing_evidence: No weight gain, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, or hair loss reported.
Acute rash and temporal relation to travel less typical.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Could explain fatigue but less likely given no blood loss, diet change, or pallor; myalgias/rash not explained.
opposing_evidence: No GI blood loss, no heavy menses (male), no dietary issues, no reported pallor.
Does not account for calf rash.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Systemic lupus erythematosus / early connective-tissue disease
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Fatigue, arthralgia and rash could represent autoimmune disease, but presentation and demographics less characteristic.
supporting_evidence: Diffuse joint/muscle aches, fatigue, cutaneous lesion.
opposing_evidence: Male sex, single localized rash rather than malar/photosensitive lesions, no joint swelling or other organ involvement.
